We need propose retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction for target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Interpret: It's a bicyclic? Looks like a cyclopentane fused? Actually there is a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene with a cyclopentanol bearing CF3? Wait C15 with three Fs is CF3 attached to carbon 15 which is attached to carbon 13? The structure: an alkene CH2= C( aromatic phenyl )-CH (attached to cyclopentane). The cyclopentane has OH and CF3 substituent.

Goal: propose retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction. Likely the carbonyl-ene reaction described. So forward reaction: carbonyl-ene forms from a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene intramolecularly to give the product with new C-C bond and OH. So retrosynthesis: break the C-O bond (alcohol) to carbonyl, and break the new C-C bond formed, revert alkene.

Thus propose precursor: a ketone (maybe cyclopentanone with CF3) and an alkene (the exocyclic alkene) that can undergo intramolecular carbonyl-ene to give product. The precursor likely is same skeleton but with carbonyl instead of OH and a C=C double bond instead of the new C-C bond? The product has a five-membered ring fused? Actually the product includes a five-membered ring (cyclopentanol). In carbonyl-ene, the carbonyl carbon becomes alcohol, and the alkene shifts to form new sigma bond. So precursor would be a cyclopentanone with an alkene side chain (maybe a terminal alkene) that undergoes ene reaction to give the product.

Thus propose retrosynthetic step: target -> precursor: replace OH with C=O (ketone) and break the bond between C9 and C2? The new bond formed is between C9 (chiral center) and C2 (alkene carbon). In precursor, C2 is part of alkene CH2= C-? Actually product has CH2= C(aryl)(C9...). In precursor, maybe the alkene is CH2= C-? The C9 attached to carbonyl carbon? Wait carbonyl-ene: carbonyl (C=O) reacts with alkene, the allylic hydrogen transfers to carbonyl oxygen forming OH, and new C-C bond forms between carbonyl carbon and the alkene's terminal carbon (the one bearing H). So in product, the carbonyl carbon becomes alcohol carbon (C13? Actually OH is on C13). The new C-C bond is between carbonyl carbon (C13) and the allylic carbon (C9?). In product, C13 is attached to OH and to C15 (CF3) and to C9? Actually SMILES: [C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] - So C13 is part of ring, attached to OH, attached to C15 (CF3 carbon) and part of ring. The new bond likely between C13 and C9 (the chiral carbon attached to alkene). So precursor would have carbonyl at C13 (C=O) and an alkene between C1=C2? The allylic hydrogen is on C9 (adjacent to C13). So precursor: same skeleton but C13 is carbonyl (C=O) and C9 is attached to alkene CH2= C(aryl) (no bond to C13). So the bond between C9 and C13 is broken, and carbonyl present.

Thus propose reaction template: carbonyl-ene intramolecular. Need to find template ID. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken: "alcohol", "C-C double bond"? Actually forward reaction: carbonyl-ene forms alcohol and new C-C bond, and changes C=C to C-C, C=O to C-O. So broken: "C=O", "C=C". Formed: "alcohol", "C-C". Use search.

Let's call tool.
